# 1.2.79 - secret passages, OBJECTION! aimed at the speaker, and the reports from 1.2.77 and 1.2.78

One stage of the 1.3.0 plan, E79: secret passages a GM gives a student, OBJECTION! on the HUD aimed at whoever is speaking, and
the owner's reports from the table on 1.2.77 and 1.2.78 - Daggerheart's welcome window, players and the file browser, an account
named like its student, the trial hall, and smaller things. None of it has been tried at a real table yet (Known gaps).

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **Daggerheart's welcome window stays closed.** The new world setting **Keep Daggerheart's welcome window closed for everyone**
   is on by default and is a GM's to change, with no reload. On, Daggerheart's welcome journal does not open for any account, the
   GM's included, and the module writes nothing to the world for it. Off, Daggerheart shows it as before, at the next start of an
   account that has never seen it.
3. **Players lose the file browser.** The new world setting **Keep players out of the file browser** is on by default and is a
   GM's to change, with no reload. On, Players and Trusted Players can neither browse nor upload files, clicking a portrait opens
   nothing for them, and a file browser that opens on their screen any other way closes; pictures already in the world still show.
   At the first start, while a GM is connected, the module changes Foundry's own permissions in the world: browsing and uploading
   files are taken from the Player and Trusted Player roles that held them (Trusted Players at Foundry's defaults as the harness
   models them; Foundry 14's own are not read yet: LIVE-E79-11), and the GMs get a card naming what was taken. Turning the setting
   off does not give them back: grant them again in Foundry's permissions. While it is on, a change to those two permissions is
   put back and the GMs are told; an account you give the file browser by name keeps it.
4. **A player's account gets its student.** A player account with no character, named exactly like one student (case, Polish
   letters and spaces aside, never a part of the name), gets that student as its character, and Owner of it when no other player
   owns it. It happens while a GM is connected: when the GM starts, when a player connects, and when an account or a student is
   added or renamed. There is no switch: a character you assign or clear by hand in User Configuration stays as you set it for the
   rest of the season, and in a new season an account with no character is matched again. Nothing is assigned, and the GMs get a
   card naming the accounts, when no student or several are named like the account, two accounts are named alike, the student
   belongs to another player, or the account owns another student.
5. **A player's token moved through a wall** is a new world setting, a GM's, with no reload: **Note it in the Debug log** (the
   default) or **Send the token back**. Keep the default until a table has shown that sending back puts nobody back wrongly
   (LIVE-E79-07).
6. **Give every room an ordinary entrance.** Every player sees a token go through a secret passage, as they see any token move,
   and a room that only a passage reaches gives the passage away.
7. **Settings, keys and texts.** Eight new settings (135 registered, 127 at 1.2.78): the three world switches above and five
   hidden ones, `accountCharacters` in the world (the season each player account was last seen with a character, given one or set
   by a GM) and four per browser for the passages. No new keybinding (3, as at 1.2.78). `lang/en.json` goes from 3416 to 3545
   strings (133 added, 4 removed, 4 reworded), `lang/pl.json` from 4191 to 4322 (135 added, 4 removed, 5 reworded). Texts a GM
   acts on: the card "'Keep players out of the file browser' took these permissions away: {lost}. Turning it off does not give
   them back: grant them again in Foundry's permissions.", the account cards (4, above), and, if it ever shows, "Secret passages
   cannot open here: every token stops at their walls. Check for an update of Danganronpa RPG, or turn off the modules that change
   how tokens move."

## At the table

### Secret passages, for the GM

- Room Setup has a **Passages** tab after Doors. **+ New passage**, then two clicks on a plain wall between two rooms of the floor
  on screen: where it begins and where it ends (Esc cancels). A door, a wall that stops nobody, a stretch another passage holds, a
  room on another floor and a wall of one room are refused with the reason. Give it to a student with **+** and their name. Each
  button in the tab acts at once; Apply and Cancel do not change it.
- Each row names who knows the passage and how (GM, start, shown), and who it was not yet delivered to. **At season start** is a
  second list; the season's reset gives it back and takes the rest, as its own group (29 groups now).
- **Revoke** takes it at once from a student outside the passage's rooms; for one inside them you choose **Revoke now** or
  **Revoke when they leave the room**. **Close** keeps who knows it and makes it a wall to all of them until **Open**; **Delete**
  forgets it and who knew it, after a yes. When the wall under it is moved off the passage's stretch or deleted the row says "The
  wall moved - pick it again".
- The Mastermind knows every secret passage and is not listed: the one player who plays the Mastermind, the first connected owner
  of the Mastermind's student. Another player who also owns that student knows only what the student was given or shown. A
  Monokuma's token passes every open secret passage when a GM moves it.
- On a GM's screen the map draws the floor's passages, and draws them again for another floor. `game.drpg.passages.log()` lists
  every grant, revoke, Close, Open and show, the newest first (its last 200).

### For a player whose character knows one

- The token goes through that stretch of wall as through a door; the step is a crossing like any other, charged as one. On that
  player's screen the room's outline opens a gap there. To everybody else it is a wall.
- A passage leads into somebody else's bedroom without a key; a locked door, a sealed room, being Chained and a Class Trial still
  turn the student back. Listen and a body's reach do not go through passages. The sheet lists them under **Known passages**: a
  name shows the passage on the map, and **the way is shut** means it does not open from where they stand.

### Showing a passage

- **Show the passage** shows it to another student in the same room, on the same floor, who can walk through it from then on: it
  costs no action, a GM has to be connected, and the GMs are told on a card of their own. Each player of the student shown it gets
  a card naming its two rooms; the one who showed it reads "You show {target} the secret passage."
- It is refused while the student showing it is dead, in an incident or a Monocub, or the action is locked; a dead student cannot
  be shown it. Showing it to a student who knows it already writes nothing and tells nobody else.

### The move check

- When a player's token is moved through a wall its character could not pass, a passage it does not know included, it is noted on
  the primary GM. With **Note it in the Debug log** that is a line in the Debug log and a row in `game.drpg.passages.audit()` (the
  newest 1000, the same move again within half a minute counted on one row); nothing moves.
- With **Send the token back** the token is put back where it stood, its player hears the refusal and reads "You cannot get there
  from {from}.", and the GMs are warned, once in half a minute for the same token and player: "{name}'s token was moved through a
  wall on {scene} and was sent back where it stood." A GM's own moves, a Monokuma's and the stairs pass; doors keep their own
  rules.

### OBJECTION!

- **The press.** In the Nonstop Debate a player presses OBJECTION! on the HUD's trial row. Its price - 1 action, else 1 Hope, else
  1 Sanity - is paid at the press. The button names the person before the press; when nobody has spoken it says "Nobody has spoken
  in this trial yet, so there is nobody to object to." and nothing is paid.
- **Whom it hits.** Whoever the GM's voice room hears speaking now (about a second of speech counts), else the last player who
  spoke in this trial. Only a living student of the table: never a GM, a Monocub, a student whose death has been announced, an
  account with no student, the objector or another student of the objector's player. A student whose death the GMs keep secret is,
  for the table, alive and may be objected to.
- **The bullet.** The player then has 30 seconds, counted down in the window, to choose the Truth Bullet; until then the card says
  the Objection is pending and the GM's console counts the seconds. Closing the window, letting the time run out, Back to debate,
  ending the debate or ending the trial withdraws it, its card says so, and the price is not given back. A GM's +30 s reaches the
  window. The 60 seconds start when the bullet is on the table, then the 120 s rebuttal.
- **The GM.** **Re-point** in the trial console aims a running Objection at another living student.
- **No voice room.** When the GM is not in a voice channel, the press asks "The GM is not connected to a voice channel, so name
  whom you contradict.", and nothing is charged until the name comes; the name is held to the same rules.
- **The sheet.** The bullet button there is a free Present, all trial long; it says "An Objection is raised with OBJECTION! on the
  HUD, not from the sheet. Press it, then choose your Truth Bullet." There is no OBJECTION! for a Monokuma, a Monocub or a dead
  student, and two presses make one Objection. Under Stained Glass the HUD's plates are never under 24 px (they were 22 on a
  narrow screen).

### The trial hall

- The tokens the module makes in the hall copy the school token's look - picture, size, rotation, opacity - and are always set not
  to turn as they move. The trial's event card runs no scrolling text under its clock.
- During a Class Trial every room tile shows the trial hall: the **Name**, **Picture** and **Description** given in Room Setup's
  Scenes tab, or "Class Trial". The tab says: "Everybody sees these on the room tile during the Class Trial. Write nothing secret
  here."

### Smaller fixes

- Foundry's own caret narrows the **Foundry tools** window when it collapses the sidebar. The room tile's project line no longer
  moves the name and the search tokens. The gear's **Voice** section sits between the volume sliders and the look.
- A player's Projects tray shows its title and "No projects yet." before the first project.
- Under Stained Glass the Hope die wears the Hope colour and the Despair die the Despair colour, as the badge beside them; a
  critical repaints neither. The notice card fills its pane, and Foundry's LATENCY/FPS readout is hidden for everyone in both
  themes.
- A move into another room is announced on the move itself, so the room tile changes at once. When two players own the same
  character, the tile on one screen can follow a move of several waypoints about a second and a half late.
- The voice tile shows the first speaker at once (a change of speaker still waits 250 ms), and while nobody speaks it names its
  state in one word: Connected, Connecting, Disconnected, Eclipsed, Blocked or Own window.
- The GM's fog no longer counts the rooms the Mastermind walks into.
- A User Configuration window that opens by itself while a browser starts closes; one a person opens stays (no switch).

### The handbooks

- GM: section 1 (the players' accounts; the two new switches), 9.1 (the Passages tab; the hall's name, picture and description),
  9.2 (the Mastermind and the fog), 9.5 (the voice tile's words), the new 9.6 Secret passages, 15 and 15.1 (OBJECTION!, the hall
  on the room tile, the hall's tokens), 16 (the reset's passages group, 29 groups) and 18 (the caret).
- Player: chapter 1 (the portrait), 3 (Secret passages, the hall on the room tile, the co-owner's delay, the voice word), 12
  (OBJECTION!) and 16 (the Projects tray). The Student Brochure's Class Trial line names OBJECTION! and its 30 s. Each in English
  and Polish.

## Changed

- **New files**: `scripts/passages.mjs`, `passages-gm.mjs`, `passages-tab.mjs` and `gm-overlay.mjs` (the passages: the GMs'
  records in three GM stores, each player's copy - only the open passages their own characters know, addressed to them alone - the
  cut of a known stretch out of the token's move, the tab and the GMs' overlay), `movement-audit.mjs` (the primary GM's check of a
  player's move through a wall), `trial-speakers.mjs` (who the GM's voice room hears) and `user-match.mjs`; 148 module files in
  `scripts/`, 141 at 1.2.78.
- **`scripts/enforced.mjs`** holds Daggerheart's welcome flag on each browser's copy of its account at `setup`, and
  `core.permissions` for `FILES_BROWSE` and `FILES_UPLOAD` on the primary GM from `ready`. **The Objection** is decided on the
  primary GM: the target from LiveKit's speaker list on the GM's Room (1000 ms in it without a break), or the name the player
  gives when that Room is down; the price at the press; the card filled from the GMs' bullet; withdrawn at 30 s.
- **Tests**: 32 new numbered tests, R553-R563 and R572-R592 (7 in tier 0, 25 in tier 1); next free R593. Scenario 76
  (`76-passages`) is new and in `ci`, 28 scenario files. `known-leaks.json` gains two Foundry limits of the passages
  (`foundry-passage-crossing`, `foundry-passage-only-room`), and the README's Privacy paragraph says the same. The glass harness
  and sweep read the notice frame, the caret's collapse, the project line, the voice word and the OBJECTION! plate.
- **The manifest's compatibility is unchanged**: Daggerheart `minimum` and `verified` 2.6.5, Foundry `minimum` 14.364 and
  `verified` 14.365. The skip baseline is unchanged.

## Known gaps

- Nothing here has run on a real Foundry v14. Each of these is a live check not tried yet: a passage's wall in a real drag, the
  ruler, the keyboard and a move made from code, and one-way walls (LIVE-E79-01); the move check's Debug log mode at a table, with
  no row for a lawful move (LIVE-E79-02), and Send the token back on a real server once that shows no wrong rows, with a second GM
  (LIVE-E79-07); two floors with Isometric Perspective (LIVE-E79-03); showing between two players (LIVE-E79-04); how the gap, the
  GMs' overlay and the Known passages list look in both themes, and the overlay after a floor switch (LIVE-E79-05); the GM's two
  clicks for a new passage on a real canvas (LIVE-E79-06); a Monokuma's and a GM's drag through a passage, and whether Foundry 14
  stops a GM's drag at a wall at all (LIVE-E79-08).
- Also not tried yet: Daggerheart's welcome window (LIVE-E79-09), the User Configuration window at a start (LIVE-E79-10), Foundry
  14's own file permissions for players (LIVE-E79-11), the account match on Foundry 14, with whether it refuses a player's rename
  and a player's write of a world setting (LIVE-E79-12), the hall token not turning (LIVE-E79-13), the hall on the room tile and
  the trial card's clock (LIVE-E79-14), the caret and Foundry tools (LIVE-E79-15), the Projects tray before the first project
  (LIVE-E79-16), the dice's colours, whose contrast (13.9:1 and 6.0:1) is computed, not seen (LIVE-E79-17), the notice card and
  the hidden readout (LIVE-E79-18), the room right after a move (LIVE-E79-19), the first speaker on an empty voice tile
  (LIVE-E79-20) and the voice tile's word through a reconnect (LIVE-E79-21).
- And: whom OBJECTION! hits - how soon the speaker is named, whether a second tells speech from a cough, the 30 s picker, the
  pending and withdrawn card, Re-point, and the GM in LiveKit's own window or with A/V off (LIVE-E79-22); the OBJECTION! button on
  the player's row, its tooltip, the hand under Monokuma Legacy, its held states and a double click (LIVE-E79-23); a long drag
  sent back to the room it paid for (LIVE-E79-24); the stairs and a real drag against "Revoke when they leave the room"
  (LIVE-E79-25).
- Not measured: how many updates a real drag writes (the room it paid for must survive the GMs' last 8 sightings and 60 s); a
  co-owner's route of several steps refused on the primary GM; an Eclipse or a budget changing between the GM's reading and the
  charge; a step out of a room and back within the quiet time, which revokes nothing (read only); a real reload of the browser of
  the Mastermind's player; whether a second GM's record is cut by a put-back (in LIVE-E79-07); the passage pick's distances,
  chosen, not measured. A floor changed without a new canvas does not draw the overlay again (read in the code).
- Not tested: a Re-point at a student whose death the GMs keep secret; the trial row's preview has no reading of its own for a
  co-owned or dead student.
- While the file switch is on, a player's own picture pickers for a project or in the investigation windows close too (read in the
  code, no scenario check).
- Under Monokuma Legacy the voice word stands at the tile's foot. Beside a long notice card, a second card waits parked at most
  desk sizes. A flake to watch, seen failing once and passing in other runs: the collapsed Foundry tools window at 1680x1050 under
  Stained Glass, which read 23 px once in the glass sweep.
- Known leaks whose stages have not shipped, unchanged: a secret project's name in Daggerheart's countdowns (until E43), an
  unfound trace's hidden token (until E60), and a character killed in secret heard in the main room on the voice tile (until E19).
  New Foundry limits: a token seen crossing a passage, and a room only a passage reaches.
